sources.source_result: Im–Li–Liu, Sidorenko's conjecture for subdivisions and theta substitutions: Theorem 1.3 supplies the even generalized theta case; Proposition 4.3 supplies the odd generalized theta case. Their density theorem is an external analytical dependency, not an imported Lean axiom.

definitions.probability_space: Omega is a finite set with weights mu(x)>=0 and sum_x mu(x)=1. No positivity is required for each individual weight.
definitions.kernel: U: Omega^r -> [0,1] is invariant under all coordinate permutations.
definitions.density: t(A,U)=sum_{x:V(A)->Omega} (product_v mu(x_v)) (product_{e in E(A)} U(x restricted to e)); any bijective ordering of the r vertices of e is allowed because U is symmetric.
definitions.private_expansion: For a finite simple graph J, J^[r] has original vertices V(J), plus r-2 distinct private vertices for each edge. A graph edge uv becomes the r-edge consisting of u,v and its own private vertices. Every private vertex belongs to exactly one edge.
definitions.pair_marginal: M_U(a,b)=E_{z_1,...,z_{r-2}} U(a,b,z_1,...,z_{r-2}). It is symmetric, lies in [0,1], and has weighted mean p(U).
definitions.cycle_rank: beta(A)=|E(Levi(A))|-|V(Levi(A))|+1 for the connected single atom. For J^[r] this is |E(J)|-|V(J)|+1. Counts are on actual carriers; no assembly-list count is substituted.
definitions.canonical_atom_shape: By the retained higher-uniformity canonical classification in the draft, a single atom is one r-edge or J^[r] for a finite simple bipartite two-vertex-connected graph J. The higher-uniformity shape theorem itself is not yet an accepted Lean endpoint.

theorem.quantifiers: For every integer r>=3, every single canonical obligatory r-uniform atom A with beta(A)<=2, every finite weighted probability space (Omega,mu), and every symmetric U:Omega^r->[0,1], t(A,U)>=p(U)^|E(A)|.
theorem.contrapositive: If such a single canonical atom violates the inequality for some finite weighted kernel, then beta(A)>=3.

proof.claim: For the single-edge atom beta=0 and t(A,U)=p(U).
proof.reason: Every edge vertex is sampled independently once. Its Levi graph is a star and has cycle rank zero.

proof.claim: For the cyclic atom A=J^[r], beta(A)=beta(J)>0.
proof.reason: If n=|V(J)| and m=|E(J)|, the Levi graph has n+(r-1)m vertices and rm edges. Thus beta(A)=rm-[n+(r-1)m]+1=m-n+1. Two-connectivity gives degree at least two; handshaking gives m>=n, hence beta(J)>=1.

proof.claim: If beta(J)=1, J is an even cycle on its actual carrier, of length at least four.
proof.reason: Connected Euler balance gives m=n. Since every degree is at least two and the degree sum is 2m=2n, all degrees are exactly two. Connected finite simple two-regular graph recognition produces the cycle isomorphism. Bipartiteness makes its length even.

proof.claim: If beta(J)=2, J is an actual theta graph consisting of three internally disjoint positive-length paths between two branch vertices.
proof.reason: The total degree excess above two is exactly two. Deleting an actual vertex and applying connected Euler balance yields degree(v)<=beta(J)+1=3, ruling out the alternative single degree-four vertex. Exactly two vertices have degree three. The accepted rank_two_three_paths theorem derives the internally disjoint paths and actual vertex/edge coverage from vertex-deletion connectivity and saturation; no theta presentation is inserted as a hypothesis.

proof.claim: The three theta path lengths are all even or all odd.
proof.reason: A fixed two-colouring c gives Even(length(P)) iff c(a)=c(b) for every actual a-b walk P. All three constructed paths have the same endpoints. No odd-order restriction is imposed. The simple-graph restriction allows at most one path of length one.

proof.claim: For every symmetric pair kernel M in [0,1], the core J satisfies t(J,M)>=(E M)^m.
proof.reason: The even-cycle case is classical Sidorenko. The all-even theta case follows from Im–Li–Liu Theorem 1.3; the all-odd theta case follows from Proposition 4.3. A finite weighted kernel is represented as a step graphon using intervals of lengths mu(x); zero-weight cells may be omitted. Thus the graphon statements apply exactly to finite weighted densities.

For each fixed assignment of the original core vertices, the private assignments belonging to distinct edges are disjoint independent samples. Finite Fubini factors their integrals edge by edge, giving one pair marginal per original graph edge. Averaging the core assignment proves the identity. Averaging the pair marginal proves the mean identity.
The expansion has one hyperedge for each original graph edge. Apply the graph inequality in Step 6 to M_U and substitute the exact identities of Step 7. The single-edge case was Step 1.

edge_case_review: An empty probability carrier cannot have total weight one; the weighted assumptions exclude it without an arbitrary Nonempty extra hypothesis.
Zero individual weights cause no problem; the step-graphon representation can use zero-length cells or omit them.
p=0 and p=1 require no division or limiting argument.
Single-edge beta=0 is treated separately: its two-vertex core is not two-vertex-connected under the project's >=3-vertex convention.
Two-connected cyclic cores have at least three vertices; bipartite rank-one cycles have at least four.
Both theta parity cases are retained. All-odd simple theta graphs may contain one direct length-one branch, but never two.
Isolated vertices do not change homomorphism densities; the canonical atom statement uses the active original carrier.
No inference is made from unrooted individual atom inequalities to an arbitrary one-point assembly.
